intro: Gravestone symbols can mean different things depending on the time, the place and the carver, so treat these as common readings, not rules. Tap any name to read more.

items.name: Rose
items.meaning: Often love and beauty. A rose with a broken or unopened bud is often read as a young life cut short.

items.name: Lily
items.meaning: Often purity and innocence, and sometimes resurrection. It was a common choice for women and children.

items.name: Wheat Sheaf
items.meaning: Often a long life ending at its natural close, like a finished harvest. It can also stand for bread in Christian symbolism.

items.name: Oak Leaves
items.meaning: Often strength, endurance and honor. Oak leaves with acorns can suggest a strong, steady life.

items.name: Ivy
items.meaning: Often faithfulness, friendship and memory. Ivy stays green all year, so it also stands for everlasting life.

items.name: Willow
items.meaning: Often mourning and grief. The weeping willow was very popular on Victorian-era stones, and it is often paired with an urn.

items.name: Pointing Hand
items.meaning: Often a hand pointing upward, showing the soul's journey to heaven.

items.name: Clasped Hands
items.meaning: Often a farewell between the living and the dead, or the bond of marriage. Sometimes the shirt cuffs are different, which is said to show a man and a woman.

items.name: Angel
items.meaning: Often a messenger or guardian who carries the soul to heaven.

items.name: Cherub
items.meaning: Often a winged child's head or figure. It is commonly seen on children's graves and stands for innocence.

items.name: Weeping Figure
items.meaning: Often a mourning woman, sometimes draped over a stone or urn. It stands for grief and loss, and became popular in the later 1800s.

items.name: Urn
items.meaning: Often a vessel for the spirit and a classical sign of death. It became popular with the classical revival styles of the 1800s.

items.name: Draped Urn
items.meaning: Often an urn covered with cloth. The drape is usually read as the veil between life and death, or as mourning.

items.name: Hourglass
items.meaning: Often the passing of time and the shortness of life. A winged hourglass is sometimes read as time flying.

items.name: Inverted Torch
items.meaning: Often a life put out. A torch turned downward is a common symbol for death.

items.name: Book
items.meaning: Often the Bible or the Book of Life. An open book can also show faith, learning or the record of a life.

items.name: Winged Death's Head
items.meaning: Often a skull with wings, showing death and the soul's flight. It was most common on stones from the 1700s and is less often seen on later pioneer-era stones.

items.name: Skull & Crossbones
items.meaning: Often a reminder of death. It can also appear on stones of some fraternal groups.

items.name: Broken Column
items.meaning: Often a life cut short, especially a person in their prime or the head of a family. It is also found on some fraternal stones.

items.name: Scythe
items.meaning: Often death as the reaper, and the end of life. A scythe with wheat can mean the harvest of a life.

items.name: Lamb
items.meaning: Often innocence, and very common on children's graves. It also recalls the Lamb of God in Christian symbolism.

items.name: Dove
items.meaning: Often peace, the Holy Spirit, or the soul itself. A dove carrying an olive branch can stand for peace.

items.name: Cross
items.meaning: Often Christian faith and resurrection. Crosses come in many forms, and some carry added meanings.

items.name: Anchor
items.meaning: Often hope and steadfastness. It was an early Christian symbol and is sometimes found on the graves of sailors.

items.name: Square & Compass
items.meaning: Often the emblem of the Freemasons, sometimes with a letter G in the middle.

items.name: Three Links
items.meaning: Often the emblem of the Odd Fellows (I.O.O.F.), often read as friendship, love and truth.

items.name: Tree Stump
items.meaning: Often the Woodmen of the World, a society that gave many members stone memorials shaped like tree stumps or logs. It can also suggest a life cut short.

items.name: Flush With Ground
items.meaning: A marker laid level with the grass. It is easy to miss, and often easier to mow around.

items.name: Flat Tablet / Slab
items.meaning: A low, flat or slightly sloped stone that lies close to the ground.

items.name: Obelisk / Column / Monument
items.meaning: A tall, pointed or column-shaped stone. It often marks a family plot, and often showed a family's status.

items.name: Standing (Vertical) Block / Arch / Slab
items.meaning: The classic upright headstone, with a flat, rounded or arched top.

items.name: Military Marker (Official)
items.meaning: A government-issued stone for a service member, usually with a name, rank, unit and dates.

items.name: Boulder / Rock
items.meaning: A natural stone or fieldstone, sometimes with a plaque. Rough fieldstones are often the only markers of early graves.

items.name: Above Ground (Single Interment)
items.meaning: A raised tomb for one burial, such as a box or table tomb resting on supports.

items.name: Above Ground Structure (Mausoleum, etc.)
items.meaning: A building-like tomb that can hold more than one burial.

items.name: Table Grave
items.meaning: A large, above-ground stone structure featuring a flat horizontal slab or stone block supported by legs, pedestals, or low stone walls. The body is buried in the ground beneath it.

items.name: Box Tomb
items.meaning: A rectangular, solid-sided stone structure shaped like a chest, usually with a slab on top. The burial is usually in the ground beneath it.

items.name: Ledger Stone
items.meaning: A flat, rectangular slab laid horizontally over a grave, often covering most of it and often carved with a long inscription.

items.name: Pedestal Tomb
items.meaning: A monument with a raised base (the pedestal) that holds a taller element such as an urn, column or statue. It often marks a family plot.

items.name: Sarcophagus
items.meaning: A large stone monument shaped like a coffin, shown above ground and often carved. It is often a symbolic monument, with the burial in the ground beneath it.

items.name: Cenotaph
items.meaning: A memorial to someone who is buried somewhere else, or whose body was never recovered.

items.name: Footstone
items.meaning: A small marker set at the foot of a grave, often with just initials and a year, facing the headstone at the other end.

items.name: Plot Curbing
items.meaning: A low stone border around a family plot, sometimes with posts or a gate, which marks the edge of the family's burial space.
